# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A; text not needed)

## BOOK 1 of 2: Ruth Fielding at Golden Pass (Alice B. Emerson, Cupples & Leon, 1925)

**Characters:** Ruth Fielding (girl director/scenario writer/star, Red Mill, Cheslow); Tom Cameron (Ruth's partner, Helen's twin brother, jealous of Layton Boardman); Helen Cameron (Ruth's chum, engaged to Chess Copley); Chess Copley (Helen's fiancé); Jennie Marchand "Heavy" Stone (married to Henri Marchand, a Frenchman in France); Ann Hicks; Nettie Parsons; Mary Cox "The Fox"; Mercy Curtis (lives in Cheslow); Uncle Jabez Potter (crabbed, disapproves of pictures); Aunt Alvirah Boggs (Ruth's housekeeper, calls her "my pretty"); Barclay Clayton "Bark" (escort); Mr. Hammond (president, Alectrion Film Corp.); Layton Boardman (western actor, hero; gray eyes, black hair; hurt in fall from horse); Sol Bloomberg (owner, Palatial Films; enemy); Viola Callahan (star; jumped contract for Bloomberg with Tony Martano); Charlie Reid (Bloomberg's agent); Anita Townsend and Grand (co-stars of "Snowblind"); Dave Sentner (comedian); Shepley (tall thin director, Ruth's right-hand); Ma and Pa Gowdy (Headwaters Ranch owners); Andy (gangling youth); Edith Lang (crippled actress, ex-Red Cross, leg amputated, coach); Sol Perkins (none in book 1 — ignore).

**Plot in order:**
1. Ch I: Snowblind premiere at Palace, Cheslow. Friends surprise Ruth with "S.B." yell (Briarwood Hall). Ruth speaks onstage; explosion, fire, lights out.
2. Ch II: Tom rescues Ruth from smoke behind stage. Backstory: Ruth orphan at 12, Red Mill, Briarwood Hall, "Heart of a School Girl."
3. Ch III: Outside theater; film storeroom explosion; party at hotel. Mr. Hammond arrives. Ruth announces Golden Pass, Montana, next picture.
4. Ch IV: Ruth plans; Hammond describes Golden Pass; Ann wants to go. Ruth hires/meets Layton Boardman in study; Aunt Alvirah admires him.
5. Ch V: Contract signed; Tom sulks, dislikes Boardman; Bloomberg worry. Helen and Jennie arrive.
6. Ch VI: Helen's news: Chess's uncle backs business deal (money for marriage). Tom locks Ruth's manuscript.
7. Ch VII: Ruth hires Viola Callahan (Brennan's contract, Viola jumped it). Viola talks of Tony Martano.
8. Ch VIII: Tom/Ruth quarrel over Viola's salary. Party at Red Mill; Boardman dances; Tom cuts in.
9. Ch IX: Departure to Chicago; Jennie leaves; Ruth "Adventure's in the air."
10. Ch X: Company; Chicago. Viola meets Charlie Reid (Bloomberg's agent) — suspicious.
11. Ch XI: Arrive Golden Pass; Headwaters Ranch (Ma and Pa Gowdy). Boardman breaks colt. Tom jealous.
12. Ch XII: Stampede of steers; Boardman tries to save Ruth, thrown from horse; Tom and cowboys shoot steers.
13. Ch XIII: Boardman injured (ankle); Ruth visits; Tom sees her hand in Boardman's.
14. Ch XIV: Rodeo filmed; Helen struck by spent/real bullet from careless cowboy.
15. Ch XV: Ruth tends Helen with Red Cross training; Viola's note: she and Tony go to Bloomberg.
16. Ch XVI: Ruth despairs; Mr. Hammond arrives; suggests Ruth act the lead.
17. Ch XVII: Ruth decides (after talk with Tom, who is jealous).
18. Ch XVIII: Test films; Ruth photogenic; Boardman's praise. Hammond suggests Edith Lang as coach.
19. Ch XIX: Edith Lang arrives; coaches Ruth. Tom goes to a bluff/water hole.
20. Ch XX: Tom and bear at water hole; Ruth finds him ("I'm a cowgirl").
21. Ch XXI: Avalanche planning; Ruth slips off ledge; Tom rescues her by jumping down.
22. Ch XXII: Ruth lets go; Boardman brings lariat; all rescued. Avalanche day.
23. Ch XXIII: Second explosion (dynamite house) buries cave company; Tom finds tunnel.
24. Ch XXIV: Outside rescuers; Tom leads company out through tunnel; two bears in cave.
25. Ch XXV: Tom shot/clawed by bear; Ruth's tourniquet with stick; Tom survives. Chess arrives. Boardman admits he can't love-make. Viola's film fails; Bloomberg humiliated. Ruth wins fame. THE END. Helen envious.

**Key quotes:** "Hearts of the Mountains" (Ruth's film). "Snowblind." "Heart of a School Girl."

## BOOK 2 of 2: When Oriole Traveled Westward (Amy Bell Marlowe, Grosset & Dunlap, 1921)

**Characters:** Oriole Putnam (Brazilian-raised girl from Bahia; parents Mr. Noddy (Mr. Putnam) and Mrs. Putnam "Mother"/"Sister"; girl at Littleport, MA with Mrs. Rebecca Joy in Dexter Mansion, State Street); Lyddy Ann (maid, afraid of ghosts, "worth her weight in ambergris"); Mrs. Rebecca Joy (sea-captain's widow); Nat Jardin (old lightkeeper, Harbor Island; says "cal'late," "sho"); Ma Stafford (housekeeper, Nat's); Payton Orr (substitute lightkeeper, gossip, wife, baby); Teddy Ford (curly-haired western boy, pink-white complexion, ex-Montana ranch hand, says "gee"); Harvey Langdon (Montana ranchman, Three-bar Ranch; twins' father); Myron and Marian Langdon (twins, ~4, Myron = boy, Marian "Mawyann," lisp; "Mawyann" for Marian); Sadie Brown "Brownie" (twins' nurse, Westerner, brusque, spinster); George Belden (trail foreman, courts Sadie, blue eyes); Ching Foo (Chinese cook, pidgin English, queue); Sol Perkins (ranch manager, Louisiana drawl); Hank Ridley (outlaw, black mustache, red face); Tom Mudd (dark mustache); Shaffer (mouse-colored hair, brown coat); Lenny (puncher); Long Jim (driver); Shedder Crabbe (son of Enos Crabbe, storekeeper/councilman; pet ram Jingo); May Rabey; Minnie and Flossy Payne (Busy Bees); Anson Cope (iceboat *Bluebird*, ran them down); Abel Hubbard (liveryman); Billy Bragg (cabin boy of *Adrian Marple*); Dr. Simms; Mrs. Orr; Molly (blue pony, Oriole's mount, "Molly Langdon"); Blooey (lazy pony pulling phaeton).

**Ship facts:** *Helvetia* (British steamship) collided in mid-ocean; Oriole rescued by *Adrian Marple* (Boston bound); ran aground on Camper Reef off Harbor Island. Father drowned (boat fall-block fouled). Mother picked up by sailing ship *Ellerton* (Captain Nathan Grimsby, wife; from Barnegat NJ).

**Plot in order (Vol 2):**
1. Ch I–II: Ice breaks; Oriole with twins on sled toward Harbor Light Island; *Bluebird* (Anson Cope) runs them into pool; Oriole, Myron, Marian in water; Teddy Ford dives, saves Marian, pulls Myron and Oriole out.
2. Ch III: Teddy tends at cottage; Teddy says "Harvey Langdon" is a villain; Teddy runs away.
3. Ch IV: Payton Orr gossip; Ma's remarks; Oriole worried.
4. Ch V: Langdon arrives at night, takes twins to hotel. Teddy returns to kitchen; Oriole catches him.
5. Ch VI: Teddy's story: worked Langdon ranch 3 months; accused of stealing family silver chest (brought from England by first Langdons). Ching Foo: "Three topside bad men—allee same talkee-talkee." Ridley, Shaffer, Tom Mudd suspects. Teddy's father a pocket-hunter (prospector), died.
6. Ch VII: Oriole urges Teddy to return to Montana; Teddy leaves; Langdon asks Oriole to come to Montana. Oriole talks to Langdon; he is still suspicious of Teddy.
7. Ch VIII–IX: Shedder/Jingo ram crashes Busy Bees sun-parlor; Enos Crabbe confronts Oriole with sheet "ghost." Langdon tells Oriole: parents likely lost; mother perhaps rescued by unknown tramp ship.
8. Ch X: Ram chases Enos Crabbe; Jingo made into mutton. Farewell party at Dexter Mansion. Oriole leaves for West with Langdon, twins, Sadie Brown.
9. Ch XI–XII: Train; Oriole sees Teddy in stock car (horses) at Boston/Chicago area; shouts "Are you coming?" Teddy: "by the spring round-up." Kansas City: George Belden (trail foreman). Teeman's Station; mad cow stampede; Oriole leaps with twins.
10. Ch XIII–XIV: Branding calf at range camp; "Beds!" move; Ching Foo; Hank Ridley's notes; Oriole hears Ridley, Shaffer, Mudd speak of "prospect hole" and "Three Sisters."
11. Ch XV–XVII: Molly the pony; Oriole overhears "Tom Mudd" and "Hank" in ravine; Teddy reappears (roped by Oriole); eagle episode.
12. Ch XVIII: Eagle swoops at Myron; Teddy lassos eagle; Langdon arrives, makes "new deal" with Teddy; Teddy hired.
13. Ch XIX–XX: Squaw Canyon fishing trip (Sadie, Belden, twins); Oriole catches trout, bear eaten; Belden shoots bear; Ridley and Mudd appear, say Shaffer missing.
14. Ch XXI–XXII: Oriole's Oriole-ness; Sol Perkins; 22 riding horses stolen; Oriole rides alone to Squaw Canyon.
15. Ch XXIII–XXIV: Oriole sees posse vs. Ridley and Mudd; kidnap threats; Hank snatches Sadie's pistol; Mudd and Ridley seize twins and ride to Byson's Creek waterfall; Sadie's ankle injured.
16. Ch XXV–XXVI: Oriole and Teddy follow; hidden path behind waterfall; Shaffer found; Mudd and Shaffer fight; Belden and posse arrive; Ridley escapes.
17. Ch XXVII: Oriole's gold wrist-watch (gift from Myron at New Year's party) lost at waterfall. Belden captures Shaffer and Mudd.
18. Ch XXVIII–XXIX: Telegram/ship info: *Ellerton*, Captain Nathan Grimsby, Barnegat; Langdon hides it from Oriole. Oriole returns alone to basin; sees Ridley lowering rope into old prospect-hole near Three Sisters.
19. Ch XXX: Oriole unties rope; Ridley trapped in shaft; posse rescues him; Teddy finds chest of silver wrapped in horse-blanket; Teddy cleared. Mrs. Putnam alive, arrives at Timmins Station, reunion. Sadie Brown marries George Belden. Langdon promises Mr. Langdon's new watch.

**Series notes:** Vol 2 ends with Oriole to appear in third volume "When Oriole Went to Boarding School." THE END.
